papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 4 setup and results 4.2.1, Section 5 Conclusions; skimmed Sections 2-3 theory.
papers.what_it_is: Two hybrid classical-quantum option-pricing methods that learn Fourier coefficients of a price distribution with parametrized quantum circuits.

assertions.value: The authors state that their two methods reconstruct Fourier series representations of statistical distributions from the outputs of QML models based on parametrized quantum circuits.
quotes: These approaches rely on reconstructing Fourier series representations of statistical distributions from the outputs of Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models based on Parametrized Quantum Circuits (PQCs).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own method.

assertions.value: The authors report that Method II obtains comparable precision using 10000 data samples, whereas the benchmarking Method III requires on the order of hundreds of thousands of shots to achieve high accuracy with low variability.
quotes: 10000 data samples as the benchmarking Method III
which requires on the order of hundreds of thousands of shots to achieve high accuracy with low variability
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study of the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is of samples against shots; the paper calls the number of circuit executions its empirical cost metric, so it is not a wall-clock or hardware comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that some outliers appear in the convergence results, attributed to the inherent error of the training process, particularly the random initialization of the quantum model weights, and that more experimental repetitions with statistical analysis are needed.
quotes: some outliers appear, which can be attributed to the inherent error of the training process, particularly to the randomness in the initialization of the quantum model weights
the importance of carrying out a larger number of experimental repetitions
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limitation.

papers.title_in_file: QSTAR: Quantum Selective Transfer with Adaptive Routing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section II methods, Section III results, tables, Limitations, Conclusion (plain-text extraction).
papers.what_it_is: A selective quantum transfer learning framework that routes only low-confidence samples to a quantum fallback head, tested on Fashion-MNIST.

assertions.value: The authors report that standard QTL heads reach at most 57.0% accuracy, the strongest KetGPT head in the main filtered sweep reaches 78.5% accuracy, and the strongest fixed classical head remains higher at 81.6%.
quotes: Standard QTL heads reach at most 57.0% accuracy, while the strongest KetGPT head in the main filtered sweep reaches 78.5% accuracy and 0.785 F1-score.
Although the strongest fixed classical head remains higher at 81.6%
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-seed empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: In this study no quantum head beat the best fixed classical head.

assertions.value: The authors report that on low-confidence samples KetGPT #180 improves accuracy over a parameter-matched MLP fallback by 6.82, 4.31 and 3.03 percentage points at thresholds 0.70, 0.80 and 0.90.
quotes: On low-confidence samples, KetGPT #180 improves accuracy over a parameter-matched MLP fallback by 6.82, 4.31, and 3.03 percentage points at thresholds of 0.70, 0.80, and 0.90.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-seed empirical result on one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Fashion-MNIST experiments use 5000 training samples and 1000 test samples, and that the quantum circuits are simulated with PennyLane using 100 measurement shots and parameter-shift gradients.
quotes: Quantum circuits are simulated with PennyLane using 100 measurement shots and parameter-shift gradients.
The Fashion-MNIST experiments use 5000 training samples and 1000 test samples
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that results are reported for a fixed seed without confidence intervals, so small differences such as 81.90% versus 81.6% should not be treated as statistically established improvements.
quotes: results are reported for a fixed seed without confidence intervals, so small differences such as 81.90% versus 81.6% should not be treated as statistically established improvements.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limitation.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Methods and results, Discussion; skimmed the supplement.
papers.what_it_is: Rigetti and NASA QuAIL iterative quantum heuristic that uses QAOA samples to freeze variables greedily, run on up to 72 qubits for Sherrington-Kirkpatrick problems.

assertions.value: The authors report implementing the algorithm on a programmable superconducting quantum system using up to 72 qubits for Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Ising spin glass problems, and state that it systematically outperforms its classical counterpart with respect to guaranteed output quality.
quotes: We implement this algorithm on a programmable superconducting quantum system using up to 72 qubits for solving paradigmatic SherringtonKirkpatrick Ising spin glass problems.
The quantum-classical algorithm systematically outperforms its classical counterpart, signaling a quantum enhancement with respect to its guaranteed output quality.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical hardware result from one study; the comparison is to a guarantee, not to the best classical solver.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is to the classical greedy guarantee, not to the best classical heuristics.

assertions.value: The authors state that no quantum algorithm has yet made the leap to quantum advantage in combinatorial optimization, and that classical simulations show a key challenge to reaching quantum advantage remains improving the quantum device characteristics.
quotes: Combinatorial optimization is a broadly attractive area for potential quantum advantage, but no quantum algorithm has yet made the leap.
Classical simulations of the algorithm illustrate that a key challenge to reaching quantum advantage remains improving the quantum device characteristics.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statement, not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that although empirical results show the quantum-enhanced algorithm can outperform the classical greedy threshold, proving this rigorously remains future work.
quotes: While our empirical results demonstrate that the quantumenhanced algorithm can outperform the classical greedy threshold, signaling a quantum boost, proving this rigorously remains as future work.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of a limitation.

assertions.value: The authors report that Sycamore takes about 200 seconds to sample one instance of a quantum circuit a million times, and that their benchmarks indicate the equivalent task for a state-of-the-art classical supercomputer would take approximately 10,000 years.

papers.title_in_file: Margin-Based Generalization for Quantum Machine Learning with Classical Data Encoding
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, contributions, Theorem statements, Conclusion, software note; skimmed proofs and appendices.
papers.what_it_is: Theory and simulation study extending margin-based generalization bounds for QNNs to classical data with fixed or trainable encodings.

assertions.value: The authors state that for fixed encodings the existing margin bound transfers unchanged, and that for trainable encodings they derive a bound with a two-scale covering argument adding an encoding-capacity term to the margin-dependent term.
quotes: For fixed encodings, the existing margin bound transfers unchanged.
we derive a bound using a two-scale covering argument that combines the original margin-dependent term with an additive encoding-capacity term
assertions.certainty_reason: Theoretical result proved in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that across 19,440 simulated training runs the inverse margin performs best among five baseline and two bound-derived complexity measures under two criteria, within bootstrap uncertainty.
quotes: Across 19,440 simulated training runs spanning various image datasets, circuit architectures, and optimization settings, the inverse margin performs best among five baseline and two bound-derived complexity measures
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulated study.
assertions.reader_inference: The bound-derived measures did not beat the plain inverse margin.

assertions.value: The authors state that simulations used the default.qubit statevector simulator in PennyLane, and that how hardware noise affects the findings is left as a follow-up question.
quotes: Simulations were performed with the default.qubit statevector simulator in PennyLane 0.42.3.
A natural follow-up question is how hardware noise affects these findings
